# Final Test Cases: SauceDemo Login

**App under test:** https://www.saucedemo.com/ (public practice site)

**Feature:** Login

**Built from:** 103 raw test cases generated by 4 AI tools (ChatGPT 40, Claude 32, Gemini 16, Copilot 15), merged, de-duplicated and corrected by me.

**Executed on:** ["22 Sep 2026"] | 

**Browser:** ["Chrome 153.0.8010.53 (Official Build) (64-bit), Microsoft Edge 153.0.4234.48 (Official build) (64-bit)"]

## How to read this file

- **Source** shows which AI tool(s) the case came from. "Added by me" means none of the four tools produced it.
- **Status:** ✅ Pass | ❌ Fail | 👁 Observation (works, but worth flagging)

**Confirmed messages** (verified live on the site during execution)

| Situation | Message |
|---|---|
| Wrong username or password (any mismatch) | `Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service` |
| Username empty | `Epic sadface: Username is required` |
| Password empty | `Epic sadface: Password is required` |
| Both fields empty | `Epic sadface: Username is required` (username validated first) |
| Locked-out user | `Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.` |
| Inventory opened while logged out (direct URL or back button) | `Epic sadface: You can only access '/inventory.html' when you are logged in.` |

## Note on TC-27

The observation as recorded is: a cookie tied to `/inventory.html` persisted after logout, while a different cookie (holding the logged-in username) was cleared. This is worth a closer look before it's written up as a finding, since:
- It's unclear whether the surviving cookie actually grants any access, or whether it's just leftover client-side routing state.
- Re-visiting `/inventory.html` after logout still correctly redirected to login (per TC-26), so whatever the leftover cookie does, it did **not** allow bypassing the login.

**Suggested next step:** open DevTools → Application → Cookies before and after logout, list exactly which cookie names persist, and try navigating to `/inventory.html` with that cookie present but the session cookie cleared, to see if it changes behavior. If it doesn't, this becomes a minor/no-impact observation rather than a security finding.

## Summary

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Total cases | 29 |
| ✅ Pass | 28 |
| ❌ Fail | 0 |
| 👁 Observations (pass, with a note) | 2 (TC-25 UX wording, TC-27 needs follow-up) |

**Key findings from execution:**
1. All AI-guessed error messages that weren't Gemini's were wrong. Only the exact `Epic sadface: ...` wording is correct.
2. The app does **not** trim whitespace, and both fields are case sensitive — this settles the disagreement between Copilot (expected trimming) and Gemini/Claude (expected no trimming).
3. No lockout or rate-limiting exists for repeated failed attempts — Claude's assumption of a lockout policy was incorrect.
4. A locked-out user with a wrong password gets the generic mismatch message, not the lockout message — none of the four tools tested this combination correctly.
5. Multiple accidental clicks on Login during a slow login did not cause duplicate-submission issues.
